title: Multiple simultaneous attempts to solve the posed request results in failed output.
body: ### What happened? It seems like there are multiple sub-agents trying to execute the same task, at least by looking at the repeated response messages, which then causes the resulting output to be garbage (although that is just my assumption). Let me know if (and how) I can provide any traces that would help. ### What did you expect to happen? linked_prs.title: Fix(core): Fix stream validation logic
linked_prs.body:
## TLDR

This pull request fixes a bug in the chat stream handling where an incomplete model response could be accepted if the stream ended with an empty or invalid data chunk. The validation logic is now stricter, requiring a valid `finishReason` to consider a stream complete, which prevents silent failures and ensures data integrity.

## Dive Deeper

The previous stream validation logic was overly complex and had a loophole: if a stream from the model ended with an invalid chunk (e.g., an empty text part) but didn't have a definitive `finishReason`, our code would often accept it as complete. This could result in the last part of a model's response being silently dropped, leading to an incomplete turn in the chat history.

This change refactors the validation logic to be more robust and explicit. A stream is now considered successful only if one of the following is true:
1. It contains a tool call (which can legitimately end without a `finishReason`).
2. Its final data chunk is valid AND it has a `finishReason` (like `STOP` or `MAX_TOKENS`).

This ensures that we no longer accept ambiguous or improperly terminated streams, making the chat interaction more reliable. The accompanying unit tests have been updated to assert this new, stricter behavior.
